documentNotes.title: Epigraph
documentNotes.statement:
*The implications of this research are intriguing.*
*It may be that commissioned work will, in general,*
*be less creative than work that is done out of pure interest.*

Teresa M. Amabile

**Main Problems for Science Fight 1**

documentNotes.title: Authorship
documentNotes.statement:
The problems are authored by Nikita Chernikov, Ilya Martchenko, and Evgeny Yunosov. Selected, prepared, and edited by Ilya Martchenko and Evgeny Yunosov. This official set of problems for the 10th IYNT 2022 is approved by General Council of the IYNT and can be used only at the events endorsed by the General Council of the IYNT.

Released in Minsk on August 15, 2021.

transcription.notes: Clean digital export (OpenOffice); the text layer matches the page. The page prints 17 problems: 1-6 under 'Main Problems for Science Fight 1', 7-12 under 'Main Problems for Science Fight 2', and 13-17 under 'Problems Invent Yourself for Science Fight 3'; the catalogue title list shows only 1-12 but its count is 17. The printed headings of problems 13-17 include the prefix 'Invent Yourself:' and are kept verbatim as titles. Page 1 carries an epigraph (Teresa M. Amabile); page 2 ends with an authorship note (Nikita Chernikov, Ilya Martchenko, Evgeny Yunosov; approved by the General Council of the IYNT) and 'Released in Minsk on August 15, 2021.' No points, time limit, figures or solutions are printed; these are open research problems. Problem 14 prints 'though-provoking' (evidently meant 'thought-provoking'); kept verbatim as printed. The epigraph with the Science Fight 1 heading and the closing authorship note are kept as paper.documentNotes.

problems.title: Chocolate and speed of light
problems.statement: A visual method to measure the speed of light is to place a chocolate bar in a microwave oven until chocolate starts to melt and measure the distance between hotspots. Study this effect and investigate the accuracy of the method.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Rotary phones
problems.statement: If volunteers of different age groups are challenged to dial a number on a rotary phone, it may turn out that some age groups are unfamiliar with the old technology. Obtain statistical data in controlled conditions and discuss the results.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Matches on fire
problems.statement: When the outermost match in a regular array of matches is lit, the following matches ignite one by one. Investigate the parameters that determine the speed for such a fire wave.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Microscopic swimmers
problems.statement: Investigate experimentally and theoretically the locomotion of bacterial or eukaryotic cells that use natural flagella to move in a liquid.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Frosty patterns
problems.statement: Patterns similar to frost on a winter window are obtained if magnesium sulphate in solution is deposited on a glass surface. Investigate this effect.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Ship wakes
problems.statement: The wave pattern produced by a ship moving on the water is visually similar to a Mach cone and depends on various parameters. Investigate the effect.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Clicking fingers
problems.statement: Snapping one's fingers results in a loud popping sound. Investigate the nature and properties of this sound.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Seeing through pinholes
problems.statement: An opaque sheet with regularly arranged pinholes corrects myopia similar to corrective lenses. Explain this effect and introduce parameters to describe image perception by myopic humans with and without pinhole glasses.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Parosmia
problems.statement: Misperception of existing odors is a common post-COVID side effect that may persist for months. Collect data to study and characterize this dysfunction.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Rubber bands heat engine
problems.statement: All the spokes in a bicycle wheel are replaced by rubber bands. If the rubber bands on one side of the wheel are heated, the wheel starts to rotate. Investigate this effect.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Resistant plants
problems.statement: Some plants are tolerant of freezes but others can hardly survive low temperatures. Perform experiments to investigate what plants can survive freezing temperatures.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Colored fire
problems.statement: It is easy to colorize a flame using various chemicals. Identify the chemicals needed to get a specific color and investigate what color is obtained if a mix of two chemicals is used.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Invent Yourself: Naming colors
problems.statement: A Munsell color chart can be used to survey volunteers about their perception of different colors. Suggest a problem related to color naming by humans and investigate the factors that influence how individuals categorize visible colors.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Invent Yourself: Wave optics
problems.statement: Formulate an open, though-provoking problem that concerns a phenomenon of wave optics.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Invent Yourself: Biological clock
problems.statement: Examples of timing processes in living organisms are plants opening their flowers at particular times of the day or sleep-wake cycles in humans. Propose a problem concerning rhythms and timing in the species of your choice.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Invent Yourself: Flying seeds
problems.statement: It is interesting to observe how maple seeds spin when falling to the ground, or how dandelion seeds fly away with the wind. Propose a problem about the flight of the seeds from a plant of your choice.

solution.incompleteReason: This is an open research problem; the archive contains no official solution.

problems.title: Invent Yourself: Principle of least effort
problems.statement: Propose an interesting experimental test of how a complex natural system chooses the path of least resistance in particular settings or situations.
